envelope.text: ADOPT-BOUNDED: rclrs returns an owned `Vec<TopicEndpointInfo>`; here the

why:
NOT impossible -- unimplemented. `nros/rmw_vtable.h` has carried the whole graph family as optional slots since phase-376 W4 (get_node_names, the four *_by_node forms, get_{topic,service}_names_and_types, get_{publishers,subscriptions}_info_by_topic, count_{publishers,subscribers}, node_get_graph_guard_condition), every one is `None` in the cffi backend, and no runtime wrapper or user entry point exists. Both real backends already run the machinery: the zenoh shim declares AND queries `@ros2_lv` liveliness tokens (`Ros2Liveliness::*_keyexpr`, wildcard GETs in shim/session.rs) -- the same mechanism rmw_zenoh_cpp builds its graph cache from -- and nros-rmw-cyclonedds publishes `ros_discovery_info` so `ros2 node list` can see us. We are VISIBLE in the graph and cannot READ it; only the reading half is missing. Phase 379 W3.

VERDICT (phase-417 gap-verdict pass, 2026-09-21) — ADOPT. **THE REASON ABOVE IS FALSE AND IS LEFT STANDING SO THE CORRECTION IS LEGIBLE.** It says the graph family is unimplemented — "every one is `None` in the cffi backend, and no runtime wrapper or user entry point exists", or it points at an anchor that said so. Measured against this checkout, both halves are gone. THE BACKEND HALF: phase-444 W3 landed `packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/graph_query.cpp` and Cyclone's vtable now fills ELEVEN of the twelve graph slots (`vtable.cpp:439-456`; only `node_get_graph_guard_condition` is still `nullptr`), and the zenoh shim answers `get_node_names`, `count_publishers`/`count_subscribers`, both `*_names_and_types`, `get_names_and_types_by_node` and `get_endpoint_info_by_topic` (`shim/session.rs:1393-1460`), reached through `rust_adapter.rs:513-534`. THE WRAPPER HALF: phase-381 W4 shipped all eleven entry points in ALL THREE languages — C `rclc_executor_get_*` / `rclc_executor_count_*` (spelled `nros_executor_*` then) (`nros_generated.h:4942-5110`), C++ `nros::Executor::*` (`executor.hpp:293-390`), Rust `Executor::*` (`nros-node/src/executor/spin.rs:4445-4609`).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS THE RECEIVER, and only that. Upstream hangs these off the NODE; we hang them off the executor, because the session is the executor's. So this row is a forwarder, not a feature — the same forwarder stage 2b already wrote for `cpp:Node::*`, which is why not one `cpp:Node::*` graph row is a gap while the `c:` and `rust:` ones still are. ADOPT: take upstream's name on upstream's receiver, delegating to the executor entry point that already answers it.

WHAT ANSWERS THE ZENOH HALF has a name worth using: the GRAPH CACHE (phase-381 / issue 0903) — a liveliness-token subscriber with history that replaced a per-question `z_liveliness_get`, started by `zpico_graph_cache_start` and walked by `graph_cache_for_each` (`nros-rmw-zenoh/src/shim/session.rs:222`, `:242`, `:818`). It is a GRAPH cache, not a matched-queryable cache; `service_is_ready`'s matched-server set (`shim/service.rs:1111`) is a READER of it, not the thing itself.

VERDICT (phase-444, 2026-09-22) — DIVERGENCE. **SHIPPED**: `Node::get_publishers_info_by_topic` and `Node::get_subscriptions_info_by_topic` (`packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/node.rs`) — the last two members of the graph family to reach upstream's receiver, beside the ten the same phase forwarded. The row above is right that this was a FORWARDER and not a feature.

It stays a divergence on SHAPE, which is what the ten siblings in `graph/` say: rclrs returns an owned `Vec<TopicEndpointInfo>`; the graph has no bound a caller can know, so a caller-sized buffer is an unanswerable question and an owned container needs an allocator a 128 KiB target does not have. We stream through a visitor, every `&str` BORROWED for the duration of the visit, returning `false` to stop the walk.

TWO CONTRACT POINTS the doc comment states: the walk reports what has been DISCOVERED and never blocks, so an empty answer is "nobody seen yet"; and `Err(Transport(Unsupported))` from a backend with no graph is a DIFFERENT answer from empty, never collapsed into a zero-visit `Ok` — the collapse issue 1087 already cost one entity kind over. Both pinned, and the ONE `bool` that discriminates the two sides of the single backend slot is pinned too: `MockSession::with_graph` answers the publisher and subscriber sides with different node names, types and `is_publisher` flags, so a forwarder handed the wrong side fails on its own line.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the visitor-vs-`Vec` bound, discovered-only/non-blocking, and `Unsupported`-vs-empty were in a `//` module note rustdoc does not render (and the method doc pointed at it). They are now on the method's own rustdoc.
